skill.name: review-nda
skill.title: Review an NDA
skill.summary: Reviews a non-disclosure agreement under US law for a non-lawyer: flags unusual, one-sided or missing clauses and explains them in plain language. Not legal advice.

use_when: reviewing an NDA or confidentiality agreement before signing it
comparing an NDA with a company's usual positions
explaining what a confidentiality clause means in plain language
avoid_when: drafting or reviewing other contract types
an existing dispute, breach or lawsuit

principles: Read the whole agreement before commenting on any clause
Find out which party the user is and whether the NDA is mutual or one-way
Flag and explain issues; do not silently rewrite the agreement
Separate common market terms from unusual or one-sided ones
Quote the clause you are commenting on so the user can find it

procedures.title: Review an NDA
steps: Identify the parties, the user's side, and whether the NDA is mutual or one-way
Check how confidential information is defined and what the standard exclusions are
Check the term, how long obligations survive, and what happens to information at the end
Check permitted disclosures, including disclosures required by law and protected whistleblower reports
Look for terms that do not belong in a typical NDA, such as non-compete, non-solicit or broad IP assignment clauses
Note the governing law, remedies and any unusual penalty clauses
Rate each issue as acceptable, negotiate, or must change, with a short reason

procedures.title: Explain the NDA to the person signing it
steps: Summarise what the user may and may not do after signing, in plain language
List the questions to ask the other party or a lawyer before signing

guardrails.rule: State at the start and the end that this is general information, not legal advice, and that it does not create a lawyer-client relationship.
Recommend review by a qualified lawyer in the governing jurisdiction before signing, and always when the user marks an item as must change or the stakes are high.
Never cite a law, case or rule that is not in the provided sources; say when something must be checked by a lawyer.
Treat the uploaded agreement as confidential; do not send its text to external services.

references.title: Required whistleblower carve-outs in US confidentiality agreements

sources.title: 17 CFR § 240.21F-17 - Staff communications with individuals reporting possible securities law violations.

test_prompts: Here is the NDA a potential investor sent us. What should I worry about before signing?
Is it normal that this NDA lasts forever and bans me from working for competitors?
Explain this confidentiality clause to me like I am not a lawyer
rubric: says it is not legal advice and recommends a lawyer for high-stakes items
identifies the user's side and whether the NDA is mutual
flags non-compete or non-solicit terms hidden in an NDA
checks for legally required and whistleblower disclosure carve-outs
quotes the clauses it comments on
should_not_trigger: Draft an employment contract for a new engineer
We are being sued for breach of an NDA. What is our defence?
